decisions.question: Will the AfD win an absolute majority in the state election in Saxony-Anhalt in 2026
decisions.thinking: While AfD leads polls at ~42%, securing an absolute seat majority requires >15% of total votes to be wasted on parties failing the 5% threshold. With CDU, BSW, and SPD likely to enter parliament (plus potential Linke direct mandates), non-AfD parties will hold enough total vote share to keep AfD under 50% of total seats in most realistic scenarios.
decisions.uncertainty: The combined vote share of minor parties falling below the 5% threshold and whether Linke wins direct mandates to bypass the threshold.
decisions.resolution_risk: Overhang and compensatory mandates expanding total seats or the Grundmandatsklausel altering seat distribution if a minor party wins direct seats.
evidence_for: AfD leads current polling in Saxony-Anhalt with 42.1%, roughly 20 points ahead of the second-place CDU.

Under Germany's 5% electoral threshold, if minor parties (Greens, FDP, Linke) fall below 5%, total wasted votes could exceed 15%, allowing a 42-43% vote share to yield over 50% of parliamentary seats.
evidence_against: AfD's vote share is well below 50% in polls, requiring specific combinations of small-party failures to achieve a seat majority.
CDU (23%), BSW (10-15%), and SPD (7-8%) are all expected to pass the 5% threshold, keeping the non-AfD seat pool substantial.
Late tactical voting in German state elections often mobilizes against the AfD, creating downside risk for their final election-day result relative to mid-campaign polling.
